title: Freeride
tagline: Free AI inference until it runs out — then the agent pays for itself on Hedera via x402
description:
Coding agents run on free inference tiers, and free tiers run out mid-task. The usual
answers are a paid gateway you have to adopt, or a bare x402 meter you have to wire up
yourself. FreeRide is neither.

FreeRide is a local gateway that keeps the free tier working: it fans every request
across OpenRouter, Groq, NVIDIA NIM, HuggingFace, Cerebras and your own Ollama, with
automatic failover when one rate-limits or retires a model mid-session. When free
genuinely cannot serve, the agent buys the inference it needs — itself, on Hedera, in
the same terminal, with no subscription, no top-up and no human in the loop. Free stays
free; paying is the escape hatch.

Three parts share one wallet. The gateway runs as a local daemon. A native terminal
coding agent (a fork of vercel-labs/fx) reads files, writes code and runs commands with
every model call served through it — and a paid turn says what it cost right in its
footer: "37s (↑22 ↓120) · 0.001 HBAR". And a set of always-on AI teammates ("Bots"),
each with its own computer and browser, can buy paywalled resources mid-job: under the
job's budget they pay and keep working, over it the run parks on an approval card and
waits for a human.

That last part is the argument. A bot that wakes you for every cent is not autonomous;
one that can spend without limit is not safe. A budget with a human backstop is what
makes an unattended agent trustworthy with money. The payer key never leaves the daemon,
so a prompt-injected agent can ask for a payment but cannot take the wallet.

A funded testnet payer ships in the package, so the whole thing works with no setup.
how_its_made:
The gateway is Python and FastAPI, serving five wire protocols (OpenAI, Anthropic,
OpenAI Responses, Gemini, and Vercel's fx/AI-Gateway dialect) so existing tools work
unmodified. The agent is Zig — a fork of vercel-labs/fx with FreeRide as its default
provider. The Bots are Next.js on the eve framework.

Hedera is the settlement layer. When free inference is exhausted, the daemon builds an
x402 v2 PAYMENT-REQUIRED challenge, signs it with the Hedera SDK (@x402/hedera, ECDSA
secp256k1) in a Node helper, and posts it to the Blocky402 facilitator's /verify then
/settle. That puts a CRYPTOTRANSFER on Hedera testnet — agent wallet debited, merchant
credited, facilitator covering the network fee — and only then does the paid request
run. The response carries PAYMENT-RESPONSE and the transaction id.

Two things worth calling out. First, the payer key is deliberately trapped in the
daemon: agents POST payment requirements to a localhost endpoint and get back a
ready-to-send PAYMENT-SIGNATURE, so they need no Hedera dependencies and never see the
key. That endpoint enforces its own ceiling, a network check and an optional payee
allowlist, because unlike the inference lane the caller now chooses both amount and
payee. Second, the Bot spending policy is not bolted on — eve's approval hook is an
async function with access to the tool input, so the budget check *is* the approval
gate, and spend is summed from the durable activity feed rather than a counter, so the
number enforced is the number you audit.

Hackiest bit: free-first means the cash lane is invisible whenever free works, which
made it impossible to demo without deleting your own provider keys. So there's a
runtime switch — /paid on inside the agent, flipped in the daemon's memory, deliberately
not persisted so an abandoned demo can't leave the wallet spending.
auto_summary: A multi-component local AI gateway routes model requests across free providers and uses Hedera-backed x402 payments when paid inference is required.
